solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group anaesthetic

definitions.meaning: a group of people can be called a body or company of them, as in 'one of us'
read as an adjective, an anaesthetic makes you more lacking in feeling: comparative of numb

explanation.surface: A clinical note about a set of drugs used to deaden pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced differently: NUMB-ER, comparative of numb, describing something that deadens feeling more.
explanation.definitionFit: A number can mean a collection or company of people; a numbing agent makes one more insensible.

clue.text: Everyone posh is never drunk

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: intoxicated, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A claim that no smart person ever gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the posh person but is the anagram signal; U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, loosely everyone and everything; 'the whole universe' means everybody.

clue.text: Wordy life drawing!

parts.note: a life sketched in words rather than paint: 'life' plus 'drawing' or graph, a written portrait

explanation.surface: An art class sketching a nude model, described as verbose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life drawing' suggests an art class, but read as life (Greek bios) plus drawing (graph) in words, it is an old word for a biography.
explanation.definitionFit: Biograph is an old term for a written account of a person's life, a biography.

clue.text: Tries in actual practice

indicators.note: the word for tries goes inside the other

parts.note: real means actual
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: Attempts are made during genuine training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like a rugby term but means hears a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a play or performance.

clue.text: Unreal contorted visual lie has no answer

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged
says the following letter is to be dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: A distorted image seen by the eye turns out to be false and leaves you without a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contorted' rearranges VISUAL LIE, and 'has no' says those letters are the entry plus A (answer), which is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusive is deceptive and based on illusion, hence not real.

clue.text: At the critical moment imprisoned by sentence

definitions.meaning: just before it is too late
jokingly: in the nick, British slang for prison, because of a term of time served

explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for prison, and 'doing time' is serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means only just in time, at the last possible moment.

clue.text: Why when spoken is variable

parts.note: the word 'why' said out loud is the letter Y, which in algebra stands for a variable quantity not yet found

explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x and y are unknowns; the spoken word 'why' sounds like the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a variable whose value is to be found is called an unknown.

clue.text: Independent male, unassuming but boastful

parts.note: modest means unassuming

explanation.surface: A freelance man, modest yet given to bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unassuming but boastful' looks like a contradiction; the opposite of MODEST is built from MODEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being immodest means showing off one's achievements, so bragging.

clue.text: One banishes spirits from former soldiers sitting on tomb

indicators.note: in a down answer, the earlier letters sit above the later ones

parts.note: ex means former
OR is short for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
a cist is a prehistoric stone burial chamber

explanation.surface: Veterans gathered on a grave try to drive away ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist drives out evil spirits by ritual.

clue.text: Rebound with wealthy alien seizing company

indicators.note: the outer letters grab hold of the others, holding them inside

parts.note: wealthy means rich
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A rich extra-terrestrial bounces back after taking over a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a projectile's bounce off a surface, a rebound.

clue.text: With hands on hips, regularly talk big and upset mob

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one of these words
knocked over, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands defiantly, hands on hips, boasting and riling a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of TALK BIG for AKI; 'upset' turns MOB into MBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Akimbo describes the stance with arms bent and hands resting on the hips.

clue.text: Death around third of March is a loss

indicators.note: the word for death goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: decease is a formal word for death

indicators.note: the third letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A March death is mourned as a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a reduction or diminution, so a loss in amount.

clue.text: Scandinavian governor dictates essentially

indicators.note: the letters lie at the core of the words, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: A northern European governor issues orders as part of his role.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic refers to the peoples and countries of Scandinavia and the north.

clue.text: Greek god's wickedly poisoned

indicators.note: acting in a wicked, unruly way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A deity of Greek myth has been treacherously poisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, brother of Zeus.

clue.text: Unusually old bison united with ox in offensive

indicators.note: in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aged bison teams up with an ox in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an attack noun, but it is the adjective meaning nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or objectionable.

clue.text: In delicate health, senator returns with husband

indicators.note: goes back, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

explanation.surface: An unwell senator comes home accompanied by her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: NESH is a British dialect word, chiefly northern, meaning feeble or susceptible to cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The dialect adjective describes someone weak, sickly or sensitive to cold.

clue.text: Contracted new road to be constructed around centre of Derby

indicators.note: built up anew, so these letters are put together in a fresh order
takes the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A new road around the middle of Derby has been commissioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' seems to mean hired to build; here it means made smaller. Derby is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowed means made less wide, shrunk, a synonym of contracted.

clue.text: Bolt possibly with second copier

parts.note: a printer copies documents

explanation.surface: Fasten something with a second photocopier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' seems a verb or fastener; it is Usain Bolt, the Jamaican Olympic champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt is an example of a fast short-distance runner; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Speak out almost immediately

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to state is to declare or speak out

explanation.surface: An urging to voice one's views without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is medical shorthand, from Latin statim, for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Outline of small horse climbing in South Island

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the others
in a down answer, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A sketch of a little pony making its way uphill in New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Island' looks like New Zealand's island but splits into two abbreviations; 'climbing' works only because this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief summary or outline of a story or argument.

clue.text: One present at function two hours before noon departs before middle of speech

parts.note: ten o'clock is two hours before midday, so 'at ten'
D is the abbreviation for departs, as on a timetable

indicators.note: takes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A guest arrives at ten, then leaves halfway through the speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of SPEECH is EE.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is a person who attends, someone present at an event.

clue.text: Poet William and French marshal joined Orczy's hero

parts.note: William Blake, the English poet and artist
Michel Ney, one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Two historical figures, an English poet and a Napoleonic soldier, team up with a fictional adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Orczy wrote The Scarlet Pimpernel, whose hero is Sir Percy Blakeney.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Percy, the Scarlet Pimpernel, is the protagonist of the Baroness's novels.

clue.text: One-armed outlaws?

parts.note: a fruit machine is called a one-armed robber because of its lever and the way it takes your money

explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot or fruit machine, worked by pulling a single lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandits are outlaws or robbers; the slot machine borrows the word.

clue.text: Reportedly checks rules

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a word sounding alike

parts.note: reins check or restrain a horse, and figuratively anything

explanation.surface: Hearsay that someone inspects the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigns rules over a kingdom; the verb in the third person.

clue.text: Baffle breaches in dugouts

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle them
breaches are gaps or holes

explanation.surface: A soldier's report on confusing gaps in the trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxholes are pits soldiers dig for shelter, much like dugouts.

clue.text: Possessing sex appeal is trendy!

parts.note: with means having or possessing
IT is old slang for sex appeal, as in 'the It girl'

explanation.surface: Having sex appeal makes you fashionable!
explanation.definitionFit: Being up with the latest ideas and fashions is the colloquial sense of trendy.

clue.text: Supporter of Cromwell perhaps provoked derision

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roundhead roused mockery among his enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironsides' was the nickname of Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War; 'perhaps' shows one trooper is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironside was one of the Parliamentarian cavalry men loyal to Oliver Cromwell.

clue.text: Scoffing father turned into sleazy bar

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable drinking place

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A mocking dad has gone into a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is a verb-sense noun here: a sire is a male parent, especially of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisive means mocking, ridiculing, scornful.

clue.text: Procedure could become messy over time

indicators.note: says the letters may be changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A warning that an orderly method may get untidy as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or set way of doing things.
